guide.summary: Notion documents OAuth 2.0 integrations in which each customer authorizes the app and selects pages. Customers in other workspaces require a public any-workspace integration. The permission boundary is the Read content capability, limited to pages shared with the connection and their children.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles and content of Notion pages that customers explicitly share with the integration. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.detail: Each user visits the authorization URL, selects pages in the page picker, and is redirected with a code. The app exchanges the code for an access token and refresh token, and the access token is used for requests on behalf of that user.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their own Notion accounts to the web app.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading page titles and content
findings.detail: Read content allows reading existing content in a workspace. Without it, page and content endpoints return 403. It does not grant update or insert content, so write capabilities are not required.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads titles and content of shared pages and never writes.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration with any-workspace scope
steps.detail: In the Developer portal Connections section, create a new connection and choose Any workspace so other customer workspaces can install it. Enter the redirect URI for the web app. Installation scope cannot be changed later, so create a new integration if it is wrong. Then open the Configuration tab to record the OAuth client ID and client secret; store the secret in an environment variable and never in source code.
steps.doneWhen: The integration exists with any-workspace scope, a redirect URI is set, and the client ID and secret are stored securely.

steps.title: Run the consent flow and verify the callback
steps.detail: Send a test user to the connection's authorization URL from the Configuration tab. The user sees the capability prompt, selects pages in the page picker, and clicks Allow access. Confirm the redirect to the redirect URI contains a code query parameter. If the user cancels, the redirect contains an error query parameter instead.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URI receives a code parameter after a test user selects at least one shared page.

evidence.quote: **Step 1** Navigate the user to the connection’s authorization URL. This URL is provided in the Developer portal.
If the user presses **Cancel**, they will be redirected to the redirect URI with and `error` query param added.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for tokens
steps.detail: Send the code from the redirect to the token endpoint with HTTP Basic authentication using client ID and secret, a JSON body with grant_type authorization_code, the code and the same redirect_uri. The response includes access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace details. Store all fields with the token pair.
steps.doneWhen: The token response returns an access_token and refresh_token that are stored securely.

steps.title: Read a shared page's properties
steps.detail: With the user's OAuth access_token, retrieve the shared page object. Titles appear under the title property in properties. The page response may show only 25 title mentions, so read the full title through the title property item endpoint and repeat with start_cursor set to next_cursor until has_more is false.
steps.doneWhen: The page object is returned and the title property item is read across all pages until has_more is false. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the page and property endpoints and no create, update, or workspace administration calls.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /v1/pages/{page_id}: $.properties.*.title[].plain_text (string)

### Paginated properties `title`, `rich_text`, `people`, and `relation` return a paginated list. Use this endpoint when a page response omits references. Continue with `next_cursor` until `has_more` is `false`. The next
URL is nested at `property_item.next_url`.

fields: PAGE_ID: a page the user shared
ACCESS_TOKEN: the user's OAuth access_token
PROPERTY_ID: title property ID from the page response
start_cursor: next_cursor from the previous property-item response

steps.title: Read the full page content as markdown
steps.detail: Call the markdown endpoint with markdown_version v2 for the shared page. Check the truncated flag and unknown_block_ids; re-request those block IDs through the same endpoint to fetch remaining subtrees. A 404 on a re-request means the block is not shared with the connection and should be reported as inaccessible, not retried indefinitely.
steps.doneWhen: Markdown content is returned for the page and any truncated subtrees are either fetched or reported as inaccessible. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the markdown endpoint and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown: $.truncated (boolean)
When truncation or permissions cause unknown blocks, the `truncated` field is set to `true` and the `unknown_block_ids` array contains the affected block IDs.
> [!NOTE] > > The `unknown_block_ids` array does not distinguish between truncated and inaccessible blocks. Handle `object_not_found` errors gracefully when re-fetching unknown block IDs.

fields: PAGE_ID: a page the user shared
ACCESS_TOKEN: the user's OAuth access_token
markdown_version: v2

steps.detail: Using the same access_token, request a page the user did not share. The expected result is a 404 object_not_found response. Do not attempt writes; this check is read-only.
steps.doneWhen: A page the user did not share returns 404 and no content is read.
